pull.title: test: no test run may touch the real machine (6.42.1)
pull.body:
A green test run must leave the machine it ran on exactly as it found it. This one did not. Twice in a single day the suite deleted the developer's real `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\MyClaudeCodeDesktop` autostart value, and it had been rewriting real files inside `~/.fcc` for longer than that.

Both classes come from one shape of mistake: a test redirects *part* of the machine and the code under test reaches the rest of it. `tests/cli/test_desktop_rtk.py` redirected `HOME`, which isolated the state file and left the registry live. Nine tests in `tests/runtime/test_catalogue_fanout.py` gave one harness a `tmp_path` and let the other eleven resolve into the real config directory. Review does not reliably catch a missing fixture argument, and neither does a per-run `-p` plugin — one was in place for the second incident and the file it did not `--ignore` still got through.

So the guard is now `tests/support/hermetic.py`, installed for the whole session from `pytest_configure` and re-exported by `tests/conftest.py`. No test opts in. A test can only opt *out*, explicitly, with a marker.

**Test-only.** `src/` is untouched; no runtime, CLI, setting, wire format or config-schema change.

## leak class → interceptor → mutation test → named tests fixed

| Leak class | Interceptor | Mutation test | Named tests fixed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Registry write | `hermetic.py:HermeticWinreg._check`, installed as `sys.modules["winreg"]`; covers `SetValueEx`, `SetValue`, `DeleteValue`, `CreateKey`, `DeleteKey` and `OpenKey` with write access | `test_a_registry_write_without_the_marker_fails_the_run`, `test_a_registry_delete_without_the_marker_fails_the_run`, `test_a_marked_registry_write_is_allowed_and_stays_in_memory` | `test_desktop_rtk.py::test_start_at_login_toggle_reads_disk_not_the_stale_cache` — **the test that deleted the autostart value** — and `::test_tray_enabled_toggle_reads_disk_not_the_stale_cache`; both take the shared `fake_winreg` fixture now |
| Write below a real config dir | `hermetic.py:protected_root_for` behind `builtins.open`/`io.open`, `Path.mkdir`, `os.mkdir`/`makedirs` | `test_a_write_below_the_config_directory_fails_the_run`, `test_opening_the_real_dotenv_for_writing_fails_the_run` | the nine `test_catalogue_fanout.py` cases that rewrote the real `crush/crush.json` and `cline/data/settings/providers.json` |
| Atomic rename into a real config dir | `os.replace`/`rename`/`link`/`symlink` | `test_replacing_a_file_into_the_config_directory_fails_the_run` | the same nine — the publisher writes a `*.fcc-tmp` and then `os.replace`s it |
| Staging or copy into a real config dir | `os.open` with a write flag, `shutil.copy*`/`move`/`rmtree` | `test_copying_into_the_config_directory_fails_the_run` | `test_release_updates.py::test_upgrade_refuses_a_wheel_whose_checksum_does_not_match`, the only upgrade test that neither disabled `_WINDOWS` nor redirected `_stage_dir`, so it wrote a real `~/.fcc/updates/wheel/w.whl` on every run |
| Start Menu, `%APPDATA%`, `~/.config`, `~/Library` | the same path predicate, over whole-profile roots | `test_a_start_menu_shortcut_fails_the_run` | none today — a regression fence |
| Real config-dir *reads*: the real `.env`, `requests.db`, `custom_providers.json` | `isolate_the_machine`, a per-test `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA`/`XDG_*` with `MCC_CONFIG_DIR` unset | `test_the_default_home_redirect_keeps_the_config_dir_out_of_the_real_one` | the 34 observed `.env` readers, now none: `check_legacy_home` → `_check_env` can no longer find a real home to probe |
| Config directory resolved to the real home | `pytest_runtest_teardown`, `tryfirst` so it runs before `_reset_config_dir_cache` clears what it inspects | `test_resolving_the_real_config_directory_fails_at_teardown` | the previous assertion was dead code: it never fired once across the 1619 tests that did resolve the real home |
| Browser, agent-CLI or machine-state launch | `subprocess.Popen.__init__` | `test_launching_a_browser_fails_the_run`, `test_a_marked_launch_is_allowed_through` | `test_admin_claude_config.py` and `test_admin_claude_settings.py`, which shelled out to `wsl.exe --list --quiet` to answer a question about a JSON document |
| Bind of the default server port | `socket.socket.bind` | `test_binding_the_default_server_port_fails_the_run` | none today — a regression fence around port 8082 |
| Ambient credentials changing an outcome | `tests/support/websearch_credentials.py` | — | `test_web_server_tools.py::test_explicit_missing_credentials_surfaces_config_error` and `::test_run_web_search_ddgs_failure_skips_second_ddgs_attempt`, plus three in `tests/websearch/` that asserted "nothing is configured" while reading the developer's exported `EXA_API_KEY` |
| Control — the guard is a filter, not a wall | — | `test_an_isolated_case_still_passes` | writes under `tmp_path`, a registry read, an ephemeral bind and a `python` launch all stay green |

## Design notes worth reading before review

**`MCC_CONFIG_DIR` is deliberately unset, not pointed at a shared directory.** It outranks `HOME` in `resolve_config_dir`, so the ~112 tests that redirect `HOME` themselves would assert on `tmp_path/.mcc/.env` while the application wrote somewhere else; and one directory shared across xdist workers races on `os.replace(".env.tmp" -> ".env")`, which on Windows surfaces as `PermissionError`. Per-test and `tmp_path`-derived is what makes both impossible.

**Matching is by prefix, not equality.** The 6.41.1 guard compared the config *directory* for equality, so everything one level inside it was unguarded — which is precisely the set that got damaged. The protected root is now the whole user profile rather than a list of config directories: this project's subject matter *is* other tools' configuration (`~/.codex`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.crush`, `~/.gemini`), and an enumeration goes stale the next time a harness is added. The temporary directories and the checkout are carved back out, both captured before any redirect.

**Registry reads succeed; only writes fail.** 720 tests reach the registry indirectly through `urllib.request.getproxies_registry` and `platform`. Failing those would be pure noise, so the fake answers reads from an in-memory store. An opted-in write still lands in that store — nothing in the suite reaches the real registry, marker or not.

**`HermeticityViolation` derives from `BaseException` on purpose.** `HarnessCatalogueFanoutPublisher._publish_one` catches `Exception` around the very write that damaged `~/.fcc` and turns it into a `logger.warning`, so an `AssertionError` guard was swallowed and the test stayed green while the file was written. Deriving from `BaseException` means the guard propagates through every `except Exception` in the application — which is why this PR needs no `src/` change to make the failure stick.

**The guard's own tests run a child pytest.** `tests/contracts/test_hermetic_guard.py` writes a deliberately leaking test, runs it under a child `pytest` with this plugin, and asserts that the child run *fails* and names the artefact. Asserting in-process would only test an interceptor's return value, not its effect on a test report — which is exactly how the old config-dir assertion stayed dead for three releases. The child is handed a stand-in profile under `tmp_path`, so even the tests of the guard touch nothing real.

`tests/README.md` states the contract and the three opt-out markers; `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` point at it.

## Verification

Full suite on Windows at `-n auto`: **9212 passed, 48 skipped, 0 failed**. `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` separately at `-n0`: 219 passed. Every new and changed file was also run at `-n0`, since xdist hides cross-test pollution. `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `ty` and `scripts/ci.sh --only suppressions` are clean.

`HKCU\...\Run` and `~/.fcc` were snapshotted immediately before and after the final run and diffed: the registry diff is **empty**, with `MyClaudeCodeDesktop` present and unchanged, and the only difference under `~/.fcc` is the mtime of `requests.db-wal`, written by the developer's separately running server.

commit.message:
test: no test run may touch the real machine (6.42.1)

Twice in one day a green suite deleted the developer's real
HKCU\...\Run\MyClaudeCodeDesktop autostart value, and repeated runs
rewrote real files inside ~/.fcc. Both came from the same shape of
mistake: a test redirects *some* of the machine and the code under test
reaches the rest of it. Review does not catch a missing fixture
argument, and a per-run -p plugin did not either -- one was in place for
the second incident.

tests/support/hermetic.py installs the guard for the whole session from
pytest_configure, and no test can forget to ask for it:

* every test gets a tmp_path-derived HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/
  LOCALAPPDATA/XDG_* with MCC_CONFIG_DIR unset. Not a session-wide
  static MCC_CONFIG_DIR: it outranks HOME in resolve_config_dir, which
  breaks the ~112 tests that redirect HOME themselves, and one shared
  directory makes xdist workers race on os.replace(".env.tmp" -> ".env");
* winreg is an in-memory fake for the session. Reads answer from it (720
  tests reach the registry only through urllib and platform); every
  write fails unless the test carries @pytest.mark.touches_registry, and
  even then it lands in the fake;
* builtins.open/io.open, os.open, os.replace/rename/mkdir/unlink/...,
  Path.mkdir and shutil.copy*/move/rmtree refuse any target inside the
  real user profile. By prefix, not equality: the 6.41.1 guard compared
  the config *directory* for equality, so ~/.fcc/crush/crush.json went
  straight past it. Temp directories and the checkout are carved out;
* subprocess.Popen refuses browsers, coding-agent CLIs and machine-state
  tools without @pytest.mark.spawns_process. python, pwsh, node, sh,
  git, cmd and tasklist stay allowed -- the suite runs those on purpose;
* socket.bind refuses the default server port;
* the config-dir teardown assertion is real now. It used to live in a
  fixture finaliser that ran after _reset_config_dir_cache had cleared
  what it inspected, and never fired once across 1619 tests that did
  resolve the real home. It is a tryfirst pytest_runtest_teardown.

HermeticityViolation derives from BaseException deliberately.
HarnessCatalogueFanoutPublisher._publish_one catches Exception around
the write that damaged ~/.fcc and turns it into a logger.warning, so an
AssertionError guard was swallowed and the test stayed green. No src
change is therefore needed: the guard now propagates through every
except Exception in the application.

Named tests fixed: test_desktop_rtk.py's two stale-cache toggles (they
drove the real set_start_at_login; they take the shared fake_winreg
fixture now), test_upgrade_refuses_a_wheel_whose_checksum_does_not_match
(staged w.whl into the real ~/.fcc/updates/wheel), the nine
test_catalogue_fanout.py cases that rewrote the real crush.json and
cline providers.json through the eleven harness paths their fixture did
not override, the two test_admin_claude_* files that shelled out to
wsl.exe, and five tests that inherited whatever web-search credentials
the developer had exported.

tests/contracts/test_hermetic_guard.py runs a deliberately leaking test
under a child pytest, one per leak class, and asserts the child run
fails naming the artefact -- asserting in-process would only test the
interceptor's return value, which is exactly how the old assertion
stayed dead code. The child gets a stand-in profile under tmp_path, so
the tests of the guard touch nothing real either.

tests/README.md states the contract and how to opt in.
